steps.prompt: Your friend says, “Trust me, cats are smarter than dogs.” What would make you actually believe them?

cards.title: Three kinds of evidence
cards.body: Evidence proves your topic sentence. A fact or number (“A 2022 survey found 7 out of 10 students…”). An example (“For example, our class grew 30 tomatoes”). A quote from someone who knows (“The nurse explains, “…””). Opinions are not evidence.

cards.title: Introduce it
cards.body: Lead into evidence so the reader knows where it comes from: According to…, For example…, For instance…, such as…, The scientist writes, “…”. Always name who said a quote.

cards.title: Evidence in a paragraph
cards.text: Pets make people healthier. According to one study, dog owners walk about 20 minutes more each day than people without dogs. For example, my neighbour lost weight after adopting a puppy.
cards.note: A fact with its source, then an example.

prompts: Which kind of evidence was easiest to write? Which was hardest?
Why should you always name the source of a quote?
